title: US sees highest number of measles cases in 35 years
snippet:
Earlier this year, a federal judge blocked the US government from implementing a series of sweeping changes to childhood immunisations under Kennedy's leadership, including slashing the number of recommended shots for children from 17 to 11.

To achieve herd immunity, which limits the spread of measles and protects the unvaccinated, around 95% of the population must have the shots. But vaccination rates have dipped far below that in some areas. [...] Last year, during an outbreak among the Russian and Ukrainian immigrant community in Spartanburg, South Carolina, some schools in the community had vaccination rates as low as 20%.

## Judge blocks RFK Jr's changes to US childhood vaccine schedule

## Deadly measles outbreak does little to counter vaccine scepticism in Texas

## Trump signs order to limit childhood vaccines and split MMR shots

## There's a reason child vaccination rates are falling - and it's not social media [...] The rising number of cases have come as vaccine hesitancy in the US has increased in recent years, leading to lower immunisation rates.

In November, a panel is set to decide whether the US will lose its status of having eliminated measles, which Canada lost last year.

A country loses elimination status after a year or more of continuous transmission of the same strain of the measles virus.

title: These seven states are hot spots for 2026's record measles outbreak
snippet:
In Utah, complications related to measles have ranged from pneumonia and dehydration to sepsis and shock, Axios' Erin Alberty writes.

## Texas

Texas had 803 cases in 2025 — more than any other state — but has seen far fewer this year, with the state reporting 188 in 2026.

   Vaccination rates for children have been dropping in Texas, just like the rest of the country.

## Virginia

Virginia had only six cases in 2025, but has now seen 176 in 2026. [...] The latest:As of late July, the CDC had recorded 2,318 cases for the year. The vast majority of those sickened are under 20 years old and are either unvaccinated or their status is unknown. There have been no recorded deaths.

   Measles was declared eliminated in the U.S. some 26 years ago, thanks to an effective vaccination program. 
   When more than 95% of people are vaccinated in a community, most people are protected — but vaccination coverage among kindergarteners has slipped. [...] Seven states account for the majority of measles cases in the United States, becoming hot spots for the life-threatening disease.

Why it matters:The U.S. measles case count has officially shattered last year's record — hitting levels unseen in more than three decades, according to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention datareleased Friday.

   A Johns Hopkins University tracker that compiles state and local health data signaled the new record earlier this week.

title: Childhood vaccination rates fall slightly, CDC says | AP News
snippet:
The CDC reported that 92.4% of 2025-26 kindergarteners got their required measles-mumps-rubella shots, down slightly from the previous year. Before the COVID-19 pandemic, the vaccination rate was 95% — the level that makes it unlikely that a single infection will spark a disease cluster or outbreak.

Vaccination rates also fell for polio, for the combination shot against diphtheria, tetanus and pertussis, and for the first dose of the vaccine against chickenpox.

The rate held steady for protection against hepatitis B. But that’s a vaccine given shortly after birth, and it will take a few years before recent federal efforts to upend infant hepatitis B vaccine recommendations would appear in the vaccination rates of kindergartners, Campbell said.

The vaccination numbers were posted as the U.S. experiences its worst year for measles since 1991. [...] Public health officials focus on vaccination rates for kindergartners because schools can be cauldrons for germs and launching pads for community outbreaks.

For years, those rates were high, thanks largely to school attendance mandates that required key vaccinations. All U.S. states and territories require that children attending childcare centers and schools be vaccinated against a number of diseases, including measles, mumps, polio, tetanus, whooping cough and chickenpox.

title: There are already more U.S. measles cases this year than in all of 2025 | PBS News
snippet:
Furthermore, experts say the spread might be greater than what's known because the virus is one of the most contagious known to medicine and vaccination rates nationwide have declined. National vaccination rates for measles, mumps and rubella — which dropped to 92.5% among kindergartners in the 2024-25 school year, from 95.2% in 2019-20 — obscure even lower rates in certain communities. [...] Rémy Pasco, a mathematical epidemiologist at the University of Colorado Boulder who is working on the analysis, said the undercounts were unsurprising. In the absence of an adequate community vaccination rate — 95% according to health experts — "there's just not much you can do about measles once you have it," he said. [...] In November, international health officials will meet to determine if the U.S. and Mexico have lost their measles-free status. The U.S. eliminated local measles spread in 2000 by maintaining high vaccination rates, which have fallen in recent years to below the 95% coverage needed to prevent outbreaks.
